Placed on the building the sheet itself labels 'UNION DEPOT' at 1233 Main (waiting room centre). Reference points used to fix it: (1) Main St. label and street line; (2) 12th St. at the top of the sheet; (3) the 'Driveway' south of the depot; (4) Camas Prairie R.R. main track; (5) Nez Perce County Court House, labelled across Main; (6) printed house number 1233; (7) block number 224; (8) facing house numbers 1234 and 1302. Placed at the centre of the main house in block 74. Reference points: (1) Monroe St. (north side of the block); (2) High St. (south side); (3) N. Commerce St. (east); (4) N. Pearl St. (west); (5) block number 74; (6) house numbers 400 and 402 across High St.; (7) the 1st Methodist Church label on block 15; (8) Madison St. at the top of the sheet. Held-out: (a) the set index assigns High 400–517 to sheet 11, and the north frontage of the 400 block of High is block 74, consistent with 401 High St.; (b) the building is drawn as a large two-story brick dwelling standing alone in the block with a central rooftop element marked '3' (read here as the cupola) and an attached rear wing, matching the entry's description of the house with an attached service wing. The sheet prints no name and no house number on the building itself.

The sheet prints 209–215 N. Canal at the Jefferson corner of block 12, with two separate frame dwellings. The entry itself records that the Garden Club and the architectural history give different Canal St. numbers (211 vs. 215), so which drawn building is the house cannot be fixed by address, and the sheet carries no name. Blank by rule.

The sheet shows Broadway, the bluff and the water works but no park boundary; the entry's overlook point at 101 S. Broadway cannot be placed on 1910 ground to street-width accuracy. Under-the-Hill itself is on sheet 25 (not sourced).

Placed at the centre of the footprint the sheet labels 'ST. MARY'S R.C. CATHEDRAL'. Reference points: (1) Main St. (north side of block 31); (2) S. Union St. (west); (3) S. Rankin St. (east); (4) State St. (south); (5) frontage numbers 600, 602, 604, 606 on Main; (6) 101 and 103 on S. Union; (7) the Priest's House and 'Cathedral Park' labels; (8) the Cathedral School across Main. Held-out: (a) the set's Specials index lists 'St. Mary's Cath. and School — sheet 16'; (b) the spire is drawn at the Union St. end and the apse at the east end, consistent with a church fronting Union. The name on the sheet settles the building; the 101/107 address question does not affect the point.

Placed at the centre of the building the sheet labels 'COUNTY COURT HOUSE' in block 14. Reference points: (1) W. Jackson St. (north); (2) W. Grove St. (south); (3) N. Monroe St. (west); (4) N. Cherry St. (east); (5) block number 14; (6) the four W.C. octagons at the square's corners; (7) the County Jail across Grove; (8) St. Mary's Church across Cherry. Held-out: (a) the set's Specials index lists 'County Court House and Jail — sheet 10'; (b) the drawn building has a projecting portico on each of its four sides and a 'clock tower' note, matching the 1858 courthouse. The entry's note that county offices moved across Cherry St. in 1939 is consistent with the jail block shown across the street.

Placed in the Chartres St. front building of block 43, marked 'Court' and 'District Police Station', at the corner of St. Peter. Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) St. Peter St.; (3) Orleans/Exchange Passage line; (4) Jackson Square (block 24) across Chartres; (5) St. Louis Cathedral (block 45) next door; (6) house numbers 701 and 713 on Chartres; (7) the 'State Arsenal' label in the rear of the block; (8) block number 43. Held-out: (a) the entry's own record places the courts in the Cabildo (the Sala Capitular as the state court's courtroom) and an early police station/guardhouse on this site — matching the sheet's 'Court' and 'Police Station' labels; (b) the Cathedral's index listing ('St. Louis Catholic Cathedral — sheet 121') confirms the sheet.

Placed in the Chartres St. front building of block 46, marked 'Court', at the corner of St. Ann. Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) St. Ann St.; (3) St. Anthony's Alley (St. Anthony St.) separating it from the Cathedral; (4) Royal St.; (5) block number 46; (6) Jackson Square across Chartres; (7) 'Priests House' label inside block 46; (8) Cathedral (block 45). Held-out: (a) the entry records the Presbytère's courthouse life (courts from 1813 and later) — matching the 'Court' label; (b) symmetry with the Cabildo on the other side of the Cathedral, as on the ground.

Placed on the 'Jackson Monument' at the centre of the square (block 24); the Cathedral is drawn and labelled directly inland across Chartres in block 45 (centre ≈ x 32.5%, y 52.7%). Reference points: (1) Chartres St.; (2) Decatur St.; (3) St. Peter St.; (4) St. Ann St.; (5) the square's corner fire hydrants; (6) the 'Granite Block' paving notes on both sides; (7) block number 24; (8) the Cathedral label. Held-out: (a) Specials index 'St. Louis Catholic Cathedral — sheet 121'; (b) the square's printed bounds — Chartres, St. Ann, Decatur and St. Peter — match the entry's own description of the park's bounding streets.

Placed on the frame dwelling at 628–632 Dumaine (block 47, between Royal and Chartres). Reference points: (1) Dumaine St. label; (2) Royal St.; (3) Chartres St.; (4) St. Ann St.; (5) block number 47; (6) printed Dumaine numbers 600, 610, 612, 618, 622, 624, 628, 630, 632; (7) the 'Macaroni Factory' and 'Wood Yard' labels in the block; (8) 'Cobble Stone' paving note on Dumaine. Held-out: (a) the building is drawn as frame (yellow) marked '1½ B.B.' — one and a half stories over a brick basement — matching the entry's description of a raised cottage with a solid brick basement and brick-between-posts upper story; (b) the sheet's '122' reference across Dumaine confirms the next sheet takes the downriver side, consistent with 632 being on this (block 47) side. Point sits at the 632/630 frontage of the building.
District entry (the whole Vieux Carré). This sheet maps one part of it around Jackson Square; an area is not a point.

The entry's anchor is the Interpretive Center at 415 N. Main. The sheet prints 419 at the North St. corner and 405/403/401 toward Hill St., but no 415; the frontage between is one lumber yard. Interpolating a lot would be a guess, so no point. Useful visible features for a caption: the 'Old Mark Twain Homestead' label on Hill St. in the same block, and the Streckfus Line steamboat dock on the river.

The entry's anchor is the Bauvais-Amoureux House, 327 St. Marys Road, south of the old town. The 1929 Sanborn set (LOC sanborn04855_004) was checked and does not reach St. Mary's Road, so the USGS quadrangle is the sheet that maps this ground. At 1:62,500 the road south of town shows building dots that cannot be identified with the house to street-width accuracy. Blank by rule.
